INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. - AADX

INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. - AADX

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pomerantz LLP is investigating claims on behalf of investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. ("Applied" or the "Company") (NYSE: AADX). Such investors are advised to contact Danielle Peyton at newaction@pomlaw.com or 646-581-9980, ext. 7980.

The investigation concerns whether Applied and certain of its officers and/or directors have engaged in securities fraud or other unlawful business practices. 

[Click here for information about joining the class action]

On or around June 2, 2026, Applied conducted its initial public offering ("IPO"), selling 32.5 million shares of common stock priced at $20.00. Then, on November 11, 2026, Applied reported its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and issued full-year 2026 financial guidance. Despite reporting quarterly revenue growth, Applied lowered its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to a range of $660 million to $670 million—falling below analyst consensus estimates—and projected full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $137 million to $142 million. Management disclosed that supplier constraints in specialized forgings, castings, and fasteners, alongside delayed government regulatory approvals for Apache helicopter rotor head overhauls, had forced the Company to push approximately $15 million to $20 million of high-margin rotorcraft aftermarket revenue out of the fourth quarter of 2026 and into the first half of 2027. Applied also reported that its consolidated gross profit margin compressed to 23.5% from 28.0% in the prior-year period due to program ramp costs and operational inefficiencies, while free cash flow turned negative at -$9.5 million.

On this news, Applied's stock price fell $1.42 per share, or 13.25%, to close at $9.30 per share on November 11, 2026, on heavy trading volume.

Then, on November 16, 2026, Jefferies downgraded Applied from "Buy" to "Hold", citing trimmed 2026 guidance, pushed-out margins, and component delivery delays.

Following the downgrade, Applied's stock price fell $1.57 per share, or 18.74%, to close at $6.81 per share on November 16, 2026.

data.title: Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed Against Fervo Energy Company: The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Outlines Lead Plaintiff Deadline
data.description:
Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed Against Fervo Energy Company: The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Outlines Lead Plaintiff Deadline

Lawsuit alleges Fervo Energy Company misled investors who acquired its securities on date of IPO, May 13, 2026; lead plaintiff deadline is January 18, 2027

A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Fervo Energy Company ("Fervo" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: FRVO) on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired ) Class A common stock pursuant and/or traceable to the registration statement and prospectus (collectively, the “Registration Statement”) issued in connection with the Company’s May 13, 2026 initial public offering (“IPO” or the “Offering”). Plaintiff pursues claims under Section 11 and 15 of the Securities Act of 1933 (the "Securities Act"). The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz today reported the case, Nikolov v. Fervo Energy Company, filed on November 19, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas (Case No. 4:26-cv-10141). Lead plaintiff motions in the Fervo Energy Company case are due by January 18, 2027.

If you lost money on Fervo Energy Company investments, contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz to learn more about the Fervo Energy Company class action and your potential claims under the federal securities laws before the January 18, 2027 lead plaintiff deadline.

Fervo Energy Company lawsuit key dates

  • Filed: November 19, 2026
  • Court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas
  • Class period: May 2026 IPO
  • Lead plaintiff motion deadline: January 18, 2027

What happened?

On October 6, 2026, during market hours, Morpheus Research published a report alleging that "Fervo has failed to disclose existential issues related to inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline, excessive water loss, seismicity-related equipment damage, transmission capacity, and ballooning costs. In some cases, Fervo appears to have presented altered data and made material misstatements to investors, including in its [initial public offering] registration statement filed with the [United States Securities and Exchange Commission].”

By the commencement of this action, the Company’s stock price had closed as low as $7.79 per share, a more than 71% decline from the $27 per share IPO price.

What is the Fervo Energy Company class action about?

The Fervo Energy Company securities lawsuit alleges that, throughout the class period, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Fervo Energy Company's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) that Fervo’s pilot plant was experiencing inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline; (2) that Fervo’s EGS operations were experiencing significant injected water loss at a level above the rate the Company’s commercial plans required; (3) that Fervo’s drilling costs were not declining as represented, including as misleadingly represented given previously published data; (4) that Fervo lacked sufficient transmission capacity to deliver power to its California customers as planned, including the transmission path underlying the Company’s approximately 290 MW of rights which was scheduled for retirement before Cape Station Phase II’s targeted 2028 COD; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Fervo Energy Company's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Fervo Energy Company securities during the class period may ask the Court, no later than January 18, 2027, to appoint them lead plaintiff in this putative class action.

"According to the complaint filed against Fervo Energy Company, the Company, among other things, failed to disclose that that Fervo’s pilot plant was experiencing inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline. Now that the case has been filed, the January 18, 2027 deadline is the date investors who bought during the class period should know," said Frank R. Cruz of The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz.

What should Fervo Energy Company investors do now?

The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz can help Fervo Energy Company investors evaluate potential claims to recover their losses. To learn more, visit the Fervo Energy Company case page, email info@frankcruzlaw.com, or call 310-914-5007.

If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.

Fervo Energy Company investors need not take any action at this time to be class members. Investors may retain counsel of their choice or take no action and remain absent class members. No class has been certified yet in the Fervo Energy Company case.

Questions and answers about the Fervo Energy Company class action

Who is eligible? Investors who bought Fervo Energy Company securities on May 13, 2026 and lost money may be class members in the Fervo Energy Company securities lawsuit.

What does a lead plaintiff do? The lead plaintiff is appointed by the court to represent all class members and direct the Fervo Energy Company class action, and lead plaintiff motions are due by January 18, 2027.

Must I act now to be part of the Fervo Energy Company class? No, Fervo Energy Company investors need not take any action at this time and may remain absent class members.

How are attorneys' fees handled? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz works on contingency, so investors pay no attorneys' fees unless there is a recovery, and any fees require court approval.

About The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz

The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz investigates and prosecutes securities fraud and corporate malfeasance class actions. With nearly 20 years of litigation experience, the firm focuses on complex securities class actions and gives each client personal, one-on-one attention throughout the legal process.

data.title: Mesoblast Wins Deloitte Tech Fast 50 Leadership & Enterprise Growth Award
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mesoblast Limited (Nasdaq:MESO; ASX:MSB), global leader in allogeneic cellular medicines for inflammatory diseases, today announced it has received the Leadership & Enterprise Growth Award at the Deloitte Technology Fast 50 Australia Awards which recognizes Australia’s fastest-growing technology companies and the founders, innovators and leaders shaping the future of the sector.

The award recognizes Mesoblast’s successful evolution to a commercial-stage biotechnology company following its U.S. launch of Ryoncil® (remestemcel-L-rknd), the first mesenchymal stromal cell therapy approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).1

“We are pleased to receive this award from Deloitte which recognizes Mesoblast's leadership excellence across innovation and scalability in the healthcare industry,” said Mesoblast Chief Executive Dr. Silviu Itescu. “The successful launch of RYONCIL has established a strong commercial foundation for Mesoblast and has enabled patients to access a life changing product. We are focused on building on that foundation, progressing our broader portfolio and delivering sustainable growth and long-term value for our shareholders.”

About Mesoblast
Mesoblast (the Company) is a world leader in developing allogeneic (off-the-shelf) cellular medicines for the treatment of severe and life-threatening inflammatory conditions. The therapies from the Company’s proprietary mesenchymal lineage cell therapy technology platform respond to severe inflammation by releasing anti-inflammatory factors that counter and modulate multiple effector arms of the immune system, resulting in significant reduction of the damaging inflammatory process.

Mesoblast’s Ryoncil® (remestemcel-L-rknd) for the treatment of steroid-refractory acute graft versus host disease (SR-aGvHD) in pediatric patients 2 months and older is the first FDA-approved mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy. Please see the full Prescribing Information at www.ryoncil.com.

Mesoblast is committed to developing additional cell therapies for distinct indications based on its remestemcel-L and rexlemestrocel-L allogeneic stromal cell technology platforms. Ryoncil® is being developed for additional inflammatory diseases including SR-aGvHD in adults and biologic-resistant inflammatory bowel disease. Rexlemestrocel-L is being developed for heart failure and chronic low back pain. The Company has established commercial partnerships in Japan, Europe and China.

About Mesoblast intellectual property: Mesoblast has a strong and extensive global intellectual property portfolio, with over 1,000 granted patents or patent applications covering mesenchymal stromal cell compositions of matter, methods of manufacturing and indications. These granted patents and patent applications provide commercial protection extending through to at least 2044 in all major markets.

About Mesoblast manufacturing: The Company’s proprietary manufacturing processes yield industrial-scale, cryopreserved, off-the-shelf, cellular medicines. These cell therapies, with defined pharmaceutical release criteria, are planned to be readily available to patients worldwide.

Mesoblast has locations in Australia, the United States and Singapore and is listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (MSB) and on the Nasdaq (MESO). For more information, please see www.mesoblast.com, LinkedIn: Mesoblast Limited and X: @Mesoblast

data.title: Shoply AI and Sports Basement Announce Scan to Chat, Turning In-Store QR Codes Into a Product Expert on Shoppers' Phones
data.description:
Shoply AI and Sports Basement Announce Scan to Chat, Turning In-Store QR Codes Into a Product Expert on Shoppers' Phones

Shoppers scan a shelf sign and get answers about the product on their phone

Shoply AI and Sports Basement today announced Scan to Chat. When a shopper in a Sports Basement store scans the QR code on a shelf sign, Shoply AI's chat assistant pops up on their phone, ready to answer questions about the product on the sign.

A shopper looking for new skis may wonder which model best suits their skill level, preferred terrain, and skiing style. Choosing the right pair often involves understanding technical details such as ski width, length, and stiffness. With Scan to Chat, shoppers can get answers to these questions immediately, even when store associates are busy helping other customers.

After scanning, shoppers see the product's photos, a short highlight of its key features, and four suggested questions they can tap to get started. Shoply AI generates these highlights and questions from product descriptions and answers using product details and store knowledge, including care guides and return policies.

“Nearly every shopper in our stores has a phone in hand, and Scan to Shoply AI Chat creates a personalized customer experience right there, so they get quick answers highly relevant to their needs. And if we don’t have their size or color in that store, they can see which Sports Basement store does,” said Anthony Biolatto, Chief Technology Officer of Sports Basement.

“During busy shopping hours, customers shouldn't have to wait for an available store associate just to get a question answered,” said Rui Jiang, co-founder and CEO of Shoply AI. “With Scan to Chat, they can simply scan a QR code and get instant, personalized answers right on their phones. It's like having a knowledgeable product expert available whenever they need one.”

Scan to Chat requires no changes to Sports Basement's existing website design. The experience is activated through QR codes on in-store shelf signs, making it easy to bring AI-powered product assistance directly to shoppers.

About Shoply AI

Shoply AI, Inc., based in San Francisco, provides AI-powered search and conversational shopping assistants for Shopify stores and other websites. To date, it has served 1,000 stores. Its technology helps shoppers discover products, get personalized recommendations, and receive instant answers based on a store's own product information and policies, supporting over 100 languages. Learn more at https://shoplyai.ai.

About Sports Basement

Founded in San Francisco in 1998, Sports Basement is a sporting goods retailer with 15 stores across California. Known for offering gear from leading brands at “basement” prices, Sports Basement also hosts thousands of community events each year. Through its Basementeers program and community partnerships, it has given more than $13 million to local charities and schools. Learn more at https://www.sportsbasement.com.

data.title: CareScout Focuses Strategic Direction on Aging Care Services
data.description:
CareScout Focuses Strategic Direction on Aging Care Services

CareScout today announced a singular focus on its aging care services business and plans to discontinue new insurance sales through CareScout Insurance Company in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The decision reflects CareScout’s belief that its services business offers the greatest opportunity to help millions of families navigate aging care for their loved ones and create long-term value for Genworth shareholders.

“We set out to make the aging journey more confident, connected, and clear, and that ambition has not changed,” said Samir Shah, CEO of CareScout. “We are choosing to focus our investment on a capital-light services business where we see the greatest opportunity for growth and long-term value creation. Together with our partners, we can help more families plan for and manage the care of aging loved ones as their needs evolve.”

CareScout brings together cost-of-care insights, care expertise, personalized guidance, and access to quality care to help families understand their needs, explore their options, and take the next steps with confidence. Building on these capabilities, the company will work with insurers, employers, advisors, and care providers to reach more families and broaden its services across the aging journey.

Existing CareScout Insurance policies remain in force with no change to servicing contacts or processes, and CareScout Insurance Company remains committed to meeting all contractual obligations. The decision is not expected to have a material impact on Genworth’s financial condition or results of operations.

About CareScout
CareScout helps older adults and their families navigate the aging journey, find, and fund quality care. Inspired by a mission to simplify and dignify the aging experience, we're building an integrated ecosystem of care and funding solutions. To learn more about CareScout, visit www.CareScout.com. data.title: San Francisco Proclaims Fromm Day as the Fromm Institute Turns 50
data.description:
San Francisco Proclaims Fromm Day as the Fromm Institute Turns 50

San Francisco Proclaims Fromm Day as the Fromm Institute Turns 50

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026

More than 960 students enrolled at the Fromm Institute this fall. In a student survey, 63 percent of respondents said they felt less isolated.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On her lunchtime walks through the University of San Francisco in 2012, Max Ferman kept seeing the same groups of older adults talking and laughing as they walked from Fromm Hall to the University Center. They disappeared in the summer and came back in the fall. "Who were these happy old people!?" she recalled wondering.

 San Francisco proclaimed Nov. 14 Fromm Day as the Fromm Institute marked 50 years of lifelong learning.

Ferman became a Fromm student in 2022 and shared that story on behalf of her fellow students at the Fromm Institute for Lifelong Learning's 50th anniversary gala on Nov. 14, 2026. Students, faculty, university leaders and supporters gathered at the McLaren Center, where the Institute received a proclamation from Mayor Daniel Lurie Office declaring Nov. 14 Fromm Day in San Francisco.

Fern Warner attended the Institute's first session in 1976 and still takes classes today. Betty Dvorson, who is about to turn 101, keeps coming to class because learning makes her happy. In a Fromm Institute student survey, 82 percent of respondents reported greater life satisfaction, 63 percent said they felt less isolated and 52 percent reported forming new social networks.

Executive Director Derek Leighnor described how those relationships take shape. A conversation that starts in class can turn into a standing lunch date or a friendship that lasts for years. When the pandemic closed classrooms in 2020, Fromm students learned to meet online so they could keep studying together and stay connected.

University of San Francisco President Salvador D. Aceves invited guests to picture an 18-year-old undergraduate heading to a first-year seminar while a 90-year-old Fromm student walked to class. Hanna and Alfred Fromm's founding vision, he said, broadened whom the university could serve and gave younger and older students a chance to learn from one another.

Rabbi Brian Lurie, chair of the Friends of the Fromm Institute Board of Directors, thanked university leaders, the board and Leighnor for sustaining the Institute.

Hanna Fromm expected about 50 people at the first open house. About 150 enrolled in the first year. This fall, more than 960 enrolled. Fifty years after that first open house, Fromm students are introducing more San Franciscans to the program at neighborhood farmers markets.

Enrollment is now open for the Fromm Institute's Winter session, which begins Jan. 11, 2027. Adults 50 and older can explore courses and enroll.

About the Fromm Institute for Lifelong Learning

Founded in 1976 at the University of San Francisco, the Fromm Institute offers daytime courses for adults 50 and older, on campus and online. Students explore art, history, literature, science and other subjects without grades, exams or homework. fromminstitute.org

data.title: Intuit Selling Mailchimp for $3.68 Billion to Berkshire Hathaway-Backed Bending Spoons — Update
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Intuit has agreed to sell its email automation platform Mailchimp for $3.68 billion to Bending Spoons, the owner of several wayward tech brands that recently attracted a major investment from Berkshire Hathaway.

The purchase price includes $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in Bending Spoons stock.

The deal comes about a month after Bending Spoons revealed that Berkshire Hathaway had invested about $930 million in the company, accumulating a 4% stake. The Milan-based company said at the time the investment would provide fresh funds to pursue additional acquisitions.

Mailchimp joins an eclectic stable of digital brands Bending Spoons owns including AOL, Everbrite, Evernote, Vimeo and others. Bending Spoons Chief Executive Luca Ferrari said his company, which went public in July, plans to invest substantially in Mailchimp once the deal closes.

Intuit said selling Mailchimp would allow it to focus on its core products, including Quickbooks, Credit Karma and TurboTax, where it is implementing more AI features. The company plans to use cash proceeds to buy back shares during fiscal 2027.

"It's better for our focus, better for our capital allocation," Chief Executive Sasan Goodarzi said on a call with investors.

The deal, which is expected to close early in 2027, came as both companies released their quarterly earnings.

Intuit reported a higher profit as revenue rose 12% to $4.35 billion in its fiscal first quarter, with results topping analyst estimates. Sales in Intuit's business-facing segment increased 15%, while its consumer-facing sales rose 7%.

Mailchimp's revenue declined 1% to $313 million in the quarter.

For the full year, Intuit said it now expected revenue between $23.08 billion to $23.37 billion, down from its prior view for $23.28 billion to $23.51 billion. It expects earnings per share of $20.12 to $20.36.

For the current second quarter, Intuit projected revenue of $4.93 billion to $4.95 billion, with earnings per share between $2.55 and $2.60. Both projections were below analysts' estimates of $5.11 billion in sales and $3.73 a share in earnings.

Bending Spoons, meanwhile, raised its outlook for the year, after reporting higher profit and revenue in the third quarter.

Shares of Intuit fell almost 10% in late trading to $297.25, while shares of Bending Spoons rose 4.3% to $43.50.
